scale: 1-5; 2 and 4 sit between the written anchors
title: Short-form video (YouTube Shorts, Reels)

anchors.1: No hook: logo, intro or slow setup; nothing makes a viewer stay.
anchors.3: A clear premise by ~3 s, but the first frame is static or generic.
anchors.5: The first frame is already the question or the action; premise lands in under 2 s with sound off.

anchors.1: Information order is random; the payoff is missing or comes first.
anchors.3: A setup → middle → payoff exists but one beat drags or repeats.
anchors.5: Every beat raises or answers a question; the payoff lands in the last 15%; no dead beat.

anchors.1: A viewer cannot say what it was about.
anchors.3: The idea is clear, but one step needs a pause or replay.
anchors.5: One idea, explained so a 12-year-old could retell it after one view.

anchors.3: Clean and consistent but generic; looks like many others.
anchors.5: Every frame composed for vertical; consistent world; motion serves the explanation.

anchors.1: VO unclear or mistimed; captions missing or wrong.
anchors.3: Clear VO and captions; music or SFX generic or too loud.
anchors.5: VO pacing matches cuts; captions exact and readable at phone size; sound design adds meaning.

anchors.1: A copy of a known creator's format and look.
anchors.3: Familiar format with one own element.
anchors.5: A recognisable own device (look, structure or voice) that passes the '500 others' test.

anchors.1: Ignores the brief or the channel's promise.
anchors.3: Fits the brief; the channel's promise is only implied.
anchors.5: Delivers the channel's promise and the brief's success test exactly.

vetoes: rights: uses footage, music or characters without a cleared right
fact: a factual error in a claim presented as true
policy: violates platform policy (misleading, unsafe, inauthentic mass-produced)
ai-tell: obvious AI artefacts a viewer would notice (hands, faces, text)
